items.stimulus: Land managers in the American West have commonly removed beaver dams, viewing the ponds behind them as water lost to evaporation that would otherwise flow downstream to farms. Hydrologists tracking several Idaho streams through dry summers found otherwise. Water held behind the dams seeped into the surrounding soil and returned to the channel gradually, so streams with dams kept flowing for weeks after streams without dams had run dry. The ponds did lose some water to the air, but they stored far more underground.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It explains the reasoning behind a common management practice, then recommends an alternative practice based on new findings.
It explains the reasoning behind a common management practice, then presents findings that undercut that reasoning.
It explains the reasoning behind a common management practice, then presents findings that confirm it apart from one exception.
It contrasts the flow of two kinds of streams, then explains why land managers have generally preferred one kind.
items.explanation: Sentence 1 gives the managers' reason for removing dams: ponds waste water. 'Found otherwise' is the turn. The rest shows that dams help streams keep flowing, which undercuts that reason. The concession at the end ('did lose some water') is part of the rebuttal and doesn't support the managers. B is correct.

C.why: You treated the last sentence's concession as the main point. Some evaporation is admitted, but the findings oppose the managers' reasoning. They don't confirm it.

D.why: The comparison of streams is one piece of evidence, not the opening move. The text also says managers remove dams, not that they prefer dammed streams.

items.stimulus: Scholars once assumed that the drone, a sustained low pitch beneath a melody, entered European folk music from the bagpipe. The account has obvious appeal, since the instrument can hardly be played without one. Yet drones appear in unaccompanied singing traditions in several regions with no history of bagpipe use. In some places, written descriptions of drone singing are older than the earliest record of the instrument. The drone, these cases suggest, may have passed from voices to bagpipes rather than the reverse.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It presents an explanation of a musical feature's origin, then cites evidence that adds to that explanation's appeal.
It presents an explanation of a musical feature's origin, then cites evidence that the feature arose separately in each tradition.
It presents an explanation of a musical feature's origin, then cites evidence that the proposed direction of influence was reversed.
It describes how a musical feature is produced, then surveys the regions where that feature remains in use today.
items.explanation: There are two turns, and the real one is the second. Sentence 2 briefly supports the old view, then 'Yet' introduces the evidence against it. That evidence doesn't just weaken the bagpipe theory. Its conclusion reverses it: the drone went from voices to bagpipes. C names that reversal.

D.why: The definition of a drone is a passing detail, and no regions are surveyed. Neither half describes how the passage is built.

items.stimulus: Fiber is known to slow the rise in blood sugar after a meal, but does it matter when the fiber is eaten? To find out, researchers served volunteers identical meals of vegetables and rice on two separate days, changing only the order of the foods. When the vegetables came first, blood sugar peaked about a third lower than when the rice came first, even though the volunteers ate the same total amount. The order of a meal, and not just its contents, appears to shape how the body handles it.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It raises a question about a factor beyond a meal's contents, then describes an experiment indicating that the factor matters less than assumed.
It reports an established finding about a nutrient, then describes several experiments whose results challenge that established finding.
It raises a question about a factor beyond a meal's contents, then explains the biological mechanism that is responsible for the effect.
It raises a question about a factor beyond a meal's contents, then describes an experiment indicating that the factor does matter.
items.explanation: The first sentence uses an accepted fact to set up an open question: does the timing of fiber matter? The experiment answers yes, since eating vegetables first lowered the blood-sugar peak. D gets both the question and the direction of the answer.

A.why: A one-third lower peak means the order matters a great deal. This choice reverses the direction of the finding.

B.why: There is one experiment, not several, and it builds on the fiber finding instead of challenging it. Reading 'known to' as the setup for a correction is a habit from other passages, and it misleads you here.

C.why: The first half fits, but the text reports a result without explaining how the body produces it. No mechanism is given, so the second half describes a step the passage never takes.

items.stimulus: The common view that a large earthquake leaves a fault "safe" for decades is half right. The rupture does release much of the stress that had built up along the segment that slipped, and that segment typically stays quiet for a long time. But the released stress does not vanish. Some of it is pushed onto the unbroken segments at either end. In 1999, for example, a magnitude 7.6 rupture on Turkey's North Anatolian Fault was followed three months later by a magnitude 7.2 earthquake just beyond its eastern end.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It accepts part of a common view about earthquakes, then describes, with an example, a consequence that the view overlooks.
It rejects a common view about earthquakes outright, then describes, with an example, an alternative that replaces it.
It accepts part of a common view about earthquakes, then explains why the view is now endorsed by most seismologists.
It describes a single earthquake sequence in Turkey, then generalizes from it to the behavior of faults everywhere.
